attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, presented as his analysis.

semantics.note: The claim is that money pressure ('all about money', 'has to... make back the money') drove the move to military and surveillance. 'Presumably' hedges only the premise about AI revenue. The causal link itself is stated firmly, so treating it as causal is right.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: financial pressure was a material cause, not the only one, and the motto line is rhetoric. The contract rightly says spending and timing alone cannot show motive.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report that the restrictions were removed. It does not tie this decision to recovering AI investment.
Google's own stated reasons: geopolitics, wider AI adoption, common standards. A company's alternative explanation does not rule out a financial motive.
The 2018 principles already allowed some military work. This covers an earlier period and says nothing about the 2025 motive.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows the policy changed on 2025-02-04, but no decision record, testimony, or sourced reporting shows that pressure to recoup AI investment drove it. Google's geopolitical explanation is incomplete and does not exclude money as a motive. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.
